latest_final: The narrator personally knew a third person and caused or contributed to that person's death. That dead person was the reader's spouse or partner, and the line "You've disappointed me so much; I'm never coming back" was the victim's sentiment toward the reader. To cover up the death and to deflect suspicion from themselves, the narrator fabricated a farewell note, repeatedly hand-copying that sentence onto a single sheet of paper in an attempt to make it seem the victim had written it and voluntarily walked away. The unnatural sevenfold repetition of the identical line was a giveaway that exposed the forgery, and that repeated copying is part of why the narrator now expects to be caught. The narrator gave this note to the reader, the victim's partner, intending the reader to believe their partner had abandoned them rather than died, a deception serving the narrator's own interest. When the reader read the note aloud to the narrator, the fabricated, repeated writing made the cover-up apparent. Realizing the deception has failed and that they are caught, the narrator sighs, "I know I'm in trouble."
